spatial_claims.claim: AB is perpendicular to reference plane P, meeting it at point A; Q is a plane passing through AB
CE is the common section (straight line) of planes P and Q, passing through A; CE lies in both P and Q
F is a point on CE distinct from A; AG is drawn in plane P perpendicular to CE at A
AB is perpendicular to CE at A (since AB perp P and CE lies in P meeting AB at A)
AB is perpendicular to AG at A (since AB perp P and AG lies in P meeting AB at A)
AG is perpendicular to both CE and AB; CE and AB are two distinct lines in plane Q meeting at A
AG is perpendicular to plane Q (by 11.4, since AG perp to two intersecting lines AB and CE in Q)
AG lies in P, is perpendicular to common section CE, and is perpendicular to Q; therefore P perp Q by D11.4

configuration_map: Point A: foot of perpendicular AB on plane P; lies in both planes P and Q; lies on common section CE. Line AB: perpendicular to plane P; lies in plane Q by hypothesis; meets P at A. Line CE: common section of P and Q; lies in both P and Q; passes through A. Line AG: lies in plane P only (not in Q); drawn perpendicular to CE at A; subsequently shown perpendicular to plane Q. Point F: on CE distinct from A; introduced in Step 3 but never used in subsequent reasoning (vestigial construction). The configuration is consistent: AB stands perpendicular to P at A, Q contains AB and intersects P in CE, AG extends within P away from CE at right angles, making AG perpendicular to both CE and AB (two lines determining Q), hence AG perpendicular to Q.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The proof correctly uses AB perpendicular to P to derive perpendicularity of AB to both CE and AG (lines in P through A). It then correctly applies 11.4 to conclude AG is perpendicular to Q (since AG is perpendicular to two intersecting lines in Q). Finally D11.4 is correctly applied to conclude P perpendicular to Q. No angle decomposition issues arise; the proof uses only right-angle perpendicularity relationships. The unused point F is a minor style issue but introduces no spatial contradiction.
